content:
maya: Kicking off bring-up for iad-edge-1 (8x A100s). Goal: full perf baseline + kernel/driver sanity before handoff. Canary planned 2026-03-20 10:00 UTC. Need list of quick checks and target p95/p99 thresholds we can sign off on.

jordan: On it. High-level run: node bootstrap -> driver/kernel checks -> microbench (latency) -> throughput sweep -> end-to-end inference sim. Will post exact commands.

liam: Quick note: watch NVLINK topology and PCIe switches — we've seen miswired cages cause 20-30% throughput drops. Add a hop test in the checklist.

ops-bot: Provisioning update: 8 nodes booted, 64 vCPUs each, 1TB NVMe local attached. All nodes passed PXE -> OS install. (provision-id: prov-iad-20260314-7)

maya: thanks. jord, can you paste the kernel/driver commands you want us to run?

jordan: sure — paste runbook snippet below. keep outputs saved to s3://redwood-ci/iad-edge/baselines/<timestamp>/

```
# ssh to first node
ssh admin@gpu-node-01
# kernel and driver
uname -r
sudo modinfo nvidia | head -n 10
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,minor_number,pstate,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv
# check for driver kernel mismatch
sudo dmesg | grep -i nvidia | tail -n 40
# nvlink topology
nvidia-smi topo -m
```

jordan: After that run microbench:

```
# micro latency ping test (small tokens)
./bench/micro_latency --model gpt-small --seq 64 --trials 200 --output /tmp/micro_lat.csv
# throughput sweep (per-GPU)
./bench/throughput_sweep --model gpt-6b --seq 1024 --batch 1,2,4,8,16 --gpus 1 --out /tmp/throughput.csv
```

liam: I'll validate kernel module flags and iommu settings. Also add this to troubleshooting: if p95 >> baseline and nvlink shows asymmetric links, run pcirescan.

```
# rescan PCI if needed
echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/bus/pci/rescan
sudo ethtool -S eth0 | head -n 20
```

tessa: I'll run the full inference sim against our CI suite and collect latency percentiles. Plan: run 30m steady-state load with realistic request distribution (mix of short/long prompts). Expected targets (per GPU): p50 tokens ~25-35ms, p95 tokens <140ms, throughput ~220-280 tok/s (model: gpt-6b quantized). If numbers diverge >20% from eu-west baseline we fail.

maya: those targets look good. where do we store the artifacts?

jordan: s3://redwood-ci/iad-edge/baselines/1816123456/ — I'll create folder and ACL so oncall can read. Also upload perf plots and raw csvs.

liam: small log from node-03 during micro run — nvlink asymmetric: link12=12GB/s link21=40GB/s — that's the kind of thing to flag.

```
[2026-03-14T09:22:10Z] node-03: nvlink: link12=12000000000, link21=40000000000
[2026-03-14T09:22:10Z] node-03: driver: 535.86, kernel: 5.19.0-45
```

maya: good catch. If we see asymmetric nvlink we'll schedule a hardware re-seat and re-run the throughput sweep. Add to runbook: re-seat, reflash BIOS, re-run.

oncall-ryan: taking handoff for the canary window at 10:00 UTC. I'll run the end-to-end smoke (3x short bursts + 1x long prompt sim) and validate latency SLOs. Ping me when baseline artifacts are uploaded.

ops-bot: Canary window reserved: 2026-03-20T10:00:00Z -> 2026-03-20T12:00:00Z (owner: oncall-ryan).

tessa: baseline run scheduled now. I'll post results once the 30m steady-state finishes. Quick heads-up: if p95 spikes correlate with GC/CPU steal, we may need to pin CPUs for qemu/k8s kubelet flags.

maya: ack. small cost note for finance: expected incremental monthly GPU cost for iad-edge-1 ~ $44k (on-demand equiv). If we plan reserved commit, let's discuss before 2026-04.

jordan: planning checklist summary I'll use for the runbook: node-level sanity, driver/kernel, nvlink topologies, micro-latency, throughput sweep, steady-state inference sim, artifact upload, handoff + canary. I'll also add a short troubleshooting matrix for asymmetric links and driver mismatches.

maya: thanks — everyone please react with :thumbsup: when you've run your checks. I'll mark this thread resolved after canary signoff.

jordan: started micro-latency now. ETA 6m.

liam: running pci/eth checks on node-02.

tessa: steady-state started. storing to s3 path above.

maya: great.
